theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: US Energy Complex is the highest-ranked trend-gated theme that is not AI/semis-adjacent and not crowded. It sits at rank 4, eligible, hurst_tag 'trend', breadth 0.727, crowding_z below +1. Given the gate's validated drawdown-control property, staying with an eligible trend theme offers better risk control than the attention-leading AI names already at the top of the leaderboard.
theses.dissent: Energy is a late-cycle value/cyclical complex; if the macro backdrop shifts to risk-off or AI-infrastructure leadership re-accelerates and absorbs the tape, energy momentum can stall despite trend eligibility.

falsifier.text: XLE lags SMH by 8% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is rank 2 and trend-eligible, but crowding_z of 1.8 marks it crowded. Crowding is a size-down caution only, never a fade — so the disciplined read is to avoid initiating fresh exposure here while leadership is extended, rather than betting against it.
theses.dissent: The theme has the strongest breadth (1.0) and a high durability_bar (0.85), so crowded positioning may simply reflect persistent institutional demand that keeps working.

falsifier.text: CIBR breaks to a new 60-day high on expanding breadth

theses.subject: Magnificent Seven
theses.thesis: Mag7 is eligible and rank 5, but its hurst_tag is 'mixed' and its proxy QQQ is heavily exposed to the already-leading AI-infrastructure complex. With absorption low (0.31) and breadth narrowing, a concentrated mega-cap tech carry offers limited marginal benefit versus the diversified energy trend for drawdown control.
theses.dissent: Mag7 has the deepest liquidity and its breadth is high (0.857); if AI-infrastructure leadership broadens, concentrated mega-cap exposure may still capture the bulk of upside.

falsifier.text: QQQ outperforms SMH by 5% over the next 30 days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
